prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json corrupts valid string values by JSON-decoding them when the parameter's annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`), turning literal strings like "null"/"true"/"123" into None/bool/int instead of leaving them as the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json corrupts valid string values by JSON-decoding them when the parameter's annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`), turning literal strings like "null"/"true"/"123" into None/bool/int instead of leaving them as the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 unwraps `Annotated[...]` before checking union members (via `_unwrap_annotated`), so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` — a common idiomatic pattern for described params — is correctly skipped. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against raw union args without unwrapping `Annotated`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped str member won't match the frozenset and the bug persists for that common case. #2032 is also broader in scope (skips pre-parsing for any str-plus-simple-type union, e.g. str|int, str|bool, str|float), which changes coercion behavior for those combinations beyond the reported str|None corruption bug, whereas #3056's docstring explicitly reasons about why the narrower str|None-only scope is correct (other simple types can legitimately result from decoding JSON, str|None cannot produce a meaningful non-str/non-None value).

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3221 does everything #3063 does but closes two edge cases #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys off str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC id 1 (int) and "1" (string) into the same key, so a legitimate distinct string id would falsely 409 against an in-flight int id of the same text; #3221's _request_stream_key() prefixes with 'i:'/'s:' to keep them distinct. clusters.pick_reason: #3056 unwraps `Annotated[...]` before checking union members (via `_unwrap_annotated`), so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` — a common idiomatic pattern for described params — is correctly skipped. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against raw union args without unwrapping `Annotated`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped str member won't match the frozenset and the bug persists for that common case. #2032 is also broader in scope (skips pre-parsing for any str-plus-simple-type union, e.g. str|int, str|bool, str|float), which changes coercion behavior for those combinations beyond the reported str|None corruption bug, whereas #3056's docstring explicitly reasons about why the narrower str|None-only scope is correct (other simple types can legitimately result from decoding JSON, str|None cannot produce a meaningful non-str/non-None value).

clusters.pick_reason: #3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using __new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restoration, so every subclass (UrlElicitationRequiredError, NoBackChannelError, etc.) round-trips correctly with no per-subclass override; its test diff explicitly adds NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError to prove the fix is general. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other MCPError subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken on pickle. #2478 also patches at the base-class level via a _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) helper that dispatches to from_error/from_error_data classmethods, but the visible diff only introduces the helper and a pragma removal on the data property without showing the corresponding __reduce__ wiring, so its completeness can't be confirmed from the diff shown, and it depends on classmethod reconstruction semantics rather than directly preserving instance state.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 replaces the single anyio.Lock with two anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) locks (one for init/token-read, one dedicated to refresh/auth-flow transitions), explicitly fixing that anyio.Lock requires same-task acquire/release while httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task -- a correctness fix beyond just reducing hold time. #3252 only relocates 'response = yield request' outside the lock block, shrinking hold time but keeping the single task-bound Lock and no separation between flow-transition and resource-request locking. #2858's diff is dominated by unrelated import/docstring cleanup (httpx2->httpx) inherited from a stale base branch, obscuring the actual lock-scope change it shares with the other two.

clusters.pick_reason: #3221 does everything #3063 does but closes two edge cases #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys off str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC id 1 (int) and "1" (string) into the same key, so a legitimate distinct string id would falsely 409 against an in-flight int id of the same text; #3221's _request_stream_key() prefixes with 'i:'/'s:' to keep them distinct. (2) #3063's bare string key means a client-supplied id equal to the literal sentinel "_GET_stream" (GET_STREAM_KEY) would collide with the standalone GET stream's slot; #3221's prefixing makes that collision structurally impossible. #3221's diff also documents both invariants inline, showing the additional cases were deliberately covered, not incidental.

clusters.pick_reason: #3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using __new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restoration, so every subclass (UrlElicitationRequiredError, NoBackChannelError, etc.) round-trips correctly with no per-subclass override; its test diff explicitly adds NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError to prove the fix is general. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving other MCPError subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken on pickle. #2478 also patches at the base-class level via a _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) helper that dispatches to from_error/from_error_data classmethods, but the visible diff only introduces the helper and a pragma removal on the data property without showing the corresponding __reduce__ wiring, so its completeness can't be confirmed from the diff shown, and it depends on classmethod reconstruction semantics rather than directly preserving instance state.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3221 does everything #3063 does but closes two edge cases #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys off str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC id 1 (int) and "1" (string) into the same key, so a legitimate distinct string id would falsely 409 against an in-flight int id of the same text; #3221's _request_stream_key() prefixes with 'i:'/'s:' to keep them distinct. (2) #3063's bare string key means a client-supplied id equal to the literal sentinel "_GET_stream" (GET_STREAM_KEY) would collide with the standalone GET stream's slot; #3221's prefixing makes that collision structurally impossible. #3221's diff also documents both invariants inline, showing the additional cases were deliberately covered, not incidental.
